Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important run chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and the players of Pakistan can be seen in a huddle near the boundary ropes as Mohammad Rizwan tries to pump them up with his words. The duo of Shubman Gill and the skipper, Rohit Sharma walk out to open the innings for India. Interesting to see if Rohit is able to move freely as he did go off the field in the first innings due to a niggle. Shaheen Afridi will get proceedings underway with the ball.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Well then, as it is seen, once the ball gets older, it becomes increasingly harder to score runs, especially for the new batters. So it will be interesting to see how Rizwan shuffles his pace attack with only one frontline spinner and two part-timers in the mix. In a high-stakes clash like this, a target of 242 might just play like 260 or a bit more, given the pressure and intensity of the contest. With the pitch expected to slow down further, it will be a challenging chase for India. So, which side of the Radcliffe Line will celebrate tonight? Will the Men in Blue send the defending champions to the brink of elimination? Or can the title holders Pakistan get the better of this Indian side? A lot is at stake and expect a more thrilling second innings. Run chase up next very shortly.

Saud Shakeel is in for a chat. He feels that he got out at the wrong time and should have spent more time in the middle. Adds that he wanted to take a chance but it did not come off for him. Shares that the ball wasn't coming onto the bat early on. Further says that the pitch is on the slower side. Mentions that early wickets will be key for them.

At one point, it seemed Pakistan were on track to push past 270, which, surely could have been a very challenging total with Rizwan and Shakeel looking solid in the middle. But those wickets came as a much-needed spark for India, just as the death overs loomed and two new batters stepped in. Salman Agha and Khushdil focused on working the singles, building a platform for a strong finish, but the duo still had plenty of work to do. However, they kept losing one too many in that phase and India just put on the squeeze after that. Khushdil Shah was the lone recognized batter left for Pakistan, with the task of shepherding the tail and also getting a total around about 250. He did strike a few lusty blows but India did not concede too many as pace off worked like a charm. Pakistan could only add 29 runs in the last five.

India went wicketless for nearly 25 overs, mirroring their struggle against Bangladesh where the spinners couldn’t break through. Pakistan, with eight wickets in hand and a good bit of batting still to follow, was in control as Shakeel reached his fifty and Rizwan closed in on his milestone. Rizwan was dropped once however, a lapse in concentration from him proved costly sooner, opening the door for India. Hardik, Jadeja, and Axar capitalized, each striking once to dismantle Pakistan’s middle order and swing the momentum back in India’s favor. Pakistan, losing Rizwan and Shakeel both in a quick span, slipped down from 151/2 to 165/5.

With two fresh batters at the crease, Pakistan entered a rebuilding phase, but the scoring rate slowed as dot balls piled up. Rizwan and Shakeel looked to steady the innings but struggled to rotate the strike consistently, with boundaries coming only occasionally. Hardik, bowling with excellent rhythm, kept the pressure on, limiting Pakistan to just 27 runs in the next ten overs without losing a wicket. As the game progressed, Jadeja and Kuldeep rushed through their overs, tightening the screws and helping India catch up on the over rate. Sensing the need to accelerate, Rizwan and Shakeel broke the lull with a flurry of boundaries around the halfway mark, injecting some much-needed momentum.

Pakistan’s openers began cautiously, negotiating the early movement while picking up timely boundaries. India’s pace duo of Shami and Rana, though slightly erratic, consistently challenged the edges. Babar Azam looked dangerous with his intent and early boundaries but fell to a stunning delivery from Hardik Pandya, while Imam-ul-Haq’s resistance ended with a poor run-out. By the end of the first Powerplay, things were brought to balance as Pakistan were 52/2, with India deploying five bowlers to keep the pressure intact.

Excellent death-over bowling from Harshit Rana. Out of the 10 balls he bowled in these last five overs or so, he conceded just 5 runs off it with a wicket. Barring Shami going for a 14-run over, this has been a tight finish from the Indians. At the pitch report, Ian Bishop and Sunil Gavaskar, both were of the opinion that any total around or above 270 would be a good defending one. So, fair to say that Pakistan would feel they are 20-25 runs short here.

Commentary.Commentary: With the anthems done, it is time for the action to commence. There are more blue shirts in the stands, but despite being outnumbered, Pakistan fans will make their presence felt. India are in a huddle near the ropes with Virat Kohli leading the pep talk. The Men in Blue take their positions, followed closely by the two Pakistani openers. With Fakhar Zaman unavailable, Babar Azam has a new opening partner in Imam-ul-Haq. Mohammad Shami will kickstart proceedings for India. A slip in place. Shami to Imam first up. Here we go!

We are inching closer to the first ball of this heavyweight clash. The stadium isn't packed just yet, but it won’t be long before every seat is taken. Right then, Rohit Sharma and Mohammad Rizwan lead their respective sides out for the national anthems. It will be India's national anthem first, followed by that of Pakistan.

The Indian skipper, Rohit Sharma says that it doesn't really matter now what they wanted to do. Mentions that this wicket looks similar to what they played on in the last game and need to bowl well. Adds that the guys in the batting lineup are experienced and this is a great opportunity to do what they do best and give their best as a team. Mentions that the run chase wasn't easy last time around but they powered through it and informs that they are playing with the same team.

The captain of Pakistan, Mohammad Rizwan says that it is a good wicket and it doesn't matter how it plays, they just want to post a good total. Says every match is important in the ICC events and hopes that the boys do well this time. Adds they are aware of the conditions and mentions about them having a good record at this venue. Says it is a new day and whatever happened in the last game is in the past. He informs about the one change. Fakhar Zaman is out and Imam-ul-Haq comes in.
India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, Axar Patel, KL Rahul (WK), Hardik Pandya, Ravindra Jadeja, Harshit Rana, Mohammad Shami, Kuldeep Yadav.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Imam-ul-Haq (In for Fakhar Zaman), Babar Azam, Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Rizwan (C/WK), Tayyab Tahir, Salman Agha, Khushdil Shah, Shaheen Afridi, Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf, Abrar Ahmed.
TOSS - Rohit Sharma calls 'heads' but it comes down as tails. Pakistan have elected to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Ian Bishop and Sunil Gavaskar are inspecting the pitch. Bishop starts and says that it is a fresh pitch and the overhead conditions are a bit warmer. Informs that it is 70 meters square on either side with 81 meters straight hit. Sunil Gavaskar joins him and expects the pitch to be on the slower side. Expects something similar to what was witnessed in the game between India and Bangladesh. Says there was a hint of turn for the wrist spinners but the finger spinners got assistance as well. Says whichever team bowls well will be able to contain the runs. Mentions that this is the pitch where six-hitting is not that easy and the score around 270 will be a defendable one here.

No matter how much either camp tries to downplay it as just another game, the reality is far from it. Given the history and stakes involved, this is undeniably a high-pressure encounter. Will the situation bring out the best in the defending champions and tournament hosts, Pakistan? Or will India make it two wins out of two and take a big step towards the semifinals? Buckle up, this one promises to be a cracker!

As for India, their win against Bangladesh wasn't convincing but having already played in Dubai, they hold a slight edge. The pitches on the square are unlikely to be too different, and with conditions expected to be slow and low, Rohit Sharma's men might have a better read on how to adapt. India’s dominance over Pakistan in ICC events is well documented, but interestingly, the Men in Green hold the edge in their Champions Trophy encounters, leading the head-to-head with three wins to two.

Not that Pakistan need a reminder, but the tournament tagline 'All on the line' perfectly sums up their situation. After a defeat to New Zealand on the opening night, Mohammad Rizwan and Co. have it all to do. Pakistan have a history of springing surprises in ICC events - either when backed into a corner or when least expected to falter. This time, it's the former, and it all comes down to which version of Pakistan shows up today.

Hello, everyone! The stage is set for a mouthwatering Group A clash on a blockbuster Sunday as arch-rivals India and Pakistan go head-to-head at the Dubai International Stadium. Last night in Lahore, Australia and England delivered an entertaining clash, with the reigning ODI World Cup champions pulling off a stunning chase. Now, it's time for two Asian powerhouses to take centre stage in a contest that promises fireworks!
... MATCH DAY ...

Rivalries in cricket, like in any sport, create electrifying moments that keep fans on the edge of their seats. While the Ashes stand as the oldest and one of the fiercest rivalries between traditional cricketing nations, there exist other matchups that command equal fervor as they occur only during prestigious ICC Tournaments and the Asia Cup. When we speak of certain rivalries, they encompass the collective passion of more than one and a half billion people, stretching far beyond geographical boundaries. Yes, this time of the year has arrived, bringing with it that match of the year, that momentous occasion for which the magnificent Dubai International Cricket Stadium stands ready to erupt with excitement. It’s India vs Pakistan in Match 5 of the ICC Champions Trophy 2025. Both teams enter this Group A clash riding on contrasting results from their opening matches. Pakistan faced a humbling defeat against New Zealand whereas India dominated their counterparts, Bangladesh. In a compact tournament like this, one defeat is enough to peg one team back and Pakistan’s tournament is on the line as they fly to Dubai to face their biggest rivals. Once considered as their fiercest weapon, Pakistan’s pace attack has given underwhelming returns, not only in the previous game but since quite a while now. The likes of Shaheen, Rauf, and Naseem pose express pace, but their sharpness seems to have gone brittle. And with just one frontline spinner in Abrar Ahmed, their spin bowling will be on the radar as to how they fare in slow conditions in Dubai. But their worries do not end here. Their batting unit has struck a huge blow with Fakhar Zaman, their premier opening batter being ruled out due to an injury. Imam-ul-Haq, another southpaw, has been named as his replacement and might be slotted as an opener. Also, a lot has been talked and discussed about the form of Babar Azam and their overall approach towards the format with the bat. With the middle order not inducing the required momentum, including Mohammad Rizwan, Pakistan has a lot to ponder. India stride into their next challenge with momentum, despite a closer-than-expected battle against Bangladesh. Mohammad Shami's roaring return with a five-fer has filled Bumrah's shoes admirably, while young Harshit Rana shows promising signs of adapting to international cricket's intensity. While Arshdeep Singh waits in the wings, along with a good bench strength including Varun Chakaravarthy and Washington Sundar as potential spinners, their bowling arsenal packs a serious punch. The batting lineup exudes confidence with Rohit Sharma finding his rhythm. Virat Kohli, too is building ominously and will be up against an opposition he absolutely loves to score, with an admirable average of 50 plus in the ODIs. Shubman Gill has been consistent and is crafting runs with the willow, fortifying the top order. With KL Rahul, being the first choice ahead of Pant, he has anchored the middle order alongside Shreyas Iyer, backed by the versatile Hardik-Jadeja combination, which makes India's batting depth look formidable. Yet eyes will be on how they do around the middle overs with the ball. In the previous game, against Bangladesh, they were a bit sloppy on the field as well, and couldn't strike a single wicket in the middle-over phase. Can the spinners provide crucial breakthroughs in that vital period to ease pressure at the death? As Dubai's pitches keep tiring up and slowing down, this strategic element could prove decisive for team combinations. India went with three proper spinners and is likely to stick with the same attack. For Pakistan, they have only one frontline spinner in Abrar Ahmed, with Khushdil Shah and Salman Agha providing support as part-timers. And it remains to be seen how they tackle the slowish conditions of Dubai with this trio, as they do not have other spin options in their squad. Four consecutive ODI victories for India against Pakistan in their last five meets, and the burning memory of 2017's Champions Trophy final defeat set the stage for an epic encounter. While history and form favor India, Pakistan has defeated India twice in Dubai which makes them tough contenders. Shaheen vs Rohit has always been a battle to watch out for with the new ball, while Virat Kohli has blown hot and cold against wrist spin, and so has Babar Azam. So, a plenty of contests within contests to watch out for. As these giants of Asian cricket prepare for battle, Dubai braces for another classic in this storied rivalry. Let the desert storm begin.
